verses.1: Which was the word of Jehovah to the prophet Jeremias regarding the nations.
verses.2: To Egypt, the army of Pharaoh, who was king of Egypt. He ruled over the river Euphrates in Carchemish. He defeated Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah.
verses.3: They built a fortress and prepared for battle.
verses.4: They banned the use of horses. Instead, they sent out patrols who stood in positions along the roads, ready to stop any intruders.
verses.5: Why did I see so many slain men? Their leaders also died. They tried to escape, but they couldn’t get out of the prison. May the Lord have mercy on them.
verses.6: Let Al-Yanus be weakened, and let the rulers be overthrown by the power of the River Euphrates. Then they will fall and be destroyed.
verses.7: Who is it that will rise up like rivers, and flow from its source?
verses.8: From Egypt, fire will rise up, and rivers will be created from water. He said, “I will take possession of a land where there are cities and their inhabitants.”
verses.9: The horses mounted up, and the chariots began to move forward. The nobles rushed out in haste, along with those who were responsible for protecting the gates and guarding the roads.
verses.10: And today is the day for the army of Jehovah to take revenge on those who have caused him harm. They will eat up the ruins and destruction. They will drink from the blood of those who have been sacrificed to Jehovah’s army in the land of Zepon, near the river Porth.
verses.11: Go up to Gilad, and take a brook from the well of Egypt for your drinking. There’s no water for you here.
verses.12: The nations heard your laughter and your cries of despair. The earth was filled with sorrow, as if two powers had been defeated together. They fell together.
verses.13: The words that Jehovah spoke to the prophet Jeremiah were these: “A prophet will come from Babylon, who will destroy the land of Egypt.”
verses.14: Speak in Egypt, and let it be heard from the heights. Let it be heard through the nostrils and ears. Say, “Arise, for your days are numbered.”
verses.15: Why did your rulers fall down, not stand firm when Jehovah was angry?
verses.16: Many people also fell down to their knees. They said, “Let us rise up and return to our own people and to the land where we were born, because of the destruction of this city.”
verses.17: They called out there for the king of Egypt, Pharaoh Shaoan. He was the one who brought the message.
verses.18: May the king, Jehovah, and his army be blessed. For they have been written down in the mountains and in the seas. They will surely come.
verses.19: All these things I have made for you to dwell in Egypt. But like a nose that is covered with dust, it will be destroyed by those who dwell there.
verses.20: A beautiful woman from Egypt, from the land of Tzafon. She came here.
verses.21: Even her wages were like the horns of a ram. Even they turned around together, but they couldn’t stand together when that day came when their punishment arrived upon them.
verses.22: Her voice is like that of a serpent; she will go along with the crowd. In their tents, they come to her, like birds flying towards her.
verses.23: They cut down their forest, as Jehovah said. For they were too numerous, and there was no end to them.
verses.24: The Egyptian girl was given into the hands of the people of Sefo.
verses.25: The LORD, the God of Israel, says: “I will punish Amun for his sins. I will also punish Pharaoh and Egypt, along with their gods and kings. I will also punish Pharaoh and those who trust in him.”
verses.26: And they were given into the hands of those who sought their souls. They were also given into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and into the hands of his servants. And after that, they would lie down in their graves from ancient times onward. Amen, LORD!
verses.27: And you, my servant Jacob, do not fear. Do not be afraid of Israel, for I will rescue you from the distance. I will bring your descendants back from the land of Shibya. Then Jacob will be safe and secure, without any danger.
verses.28: Do not be afraid, my servant Jacob! The LORD says, “I will do this to all the nations that have rejected you. But to you, I will not do this. I will not punish you in judgment. I will not abandon you.”
